svg.title: Three tests of a ranking learned from abstracts alone
svg.desc: Corpus ledger, computed-property bars, measured rank correlations, an 18-stratum historical replay and the context-word trace for CsAgGa2Se4.
svg.text: LIA / PART III / III-03 LATENT KNOWLEDGE IN MATERIALS SCIENCE
Three tests of a ranking learned from abstracts alone
Word embeddings trained on materials abstracts ranked compounds that no abstract had placed beside the word thermoelectric.
Each test reaches a different distance from text toward measurement.
No labels and no chemistry were supplied. To the algorithm a formula was a string of characters like any other word.
Power factors calculated from physical theory for
embeddings were never adjusted using these data.

that link the formula to the target word. The
prediction is the sum of these associations.
Why the links carry weight: many good thermoelectrics are chalcogenides, most need a bandgap, and thermoelectric materials
overlap heavily with optoelectronic and photovoltaic ones. The embeddings register which words occur together; they cannot
Sources: Tshitoyan et al. 2019, Unsupervised word embeddings capture latent knowledge from materials science literature, Nature 571. Bar lengths
